meta_title: podbag — a container engine with no daemon
meta_description: podbag runs Docker and OCI containers with no daemon, from one static binary. It stores images file by file, so it uses less disk and less memory. Linux, macOS and Windows.
hero_eyebrow: A different kind of container engine
hero_title: Containers with no daemon, stored file by file
hero_lead: One static binary runs your Docker and OCI images. When no container runs, nothing runs. A file that many images share is stored once and read into memory once.
term_sr: An example: install podbag with the install script, run a container that prints hello, then see that no podbag process is left running.
features_sub: Light where other engines are heavy.
f1_d: When no container runs, nothing runs.
f3_d: A file that many images share is stored once and cached once: less disk, less memory.
f4_d: A container starts in about 4 ms on Linux.
f5_d: Docker and OCI images, the docker CLI, Compose and buildx.
f6_d: The same program works both ways.
f7_d: x86_64 and arm64. Windows support is experimental.
how_sub: Three containers start, then stop. Watch the processes on the machine.
how_aria: Docker Engine runs dockerd and containerd all the time and adds a shim for each container; with no containers it still holds 203 MiB. podbag runs nothing at rest; while containers run, one small keeper watches them, and it leaves 10 seconds after the last one.
keeper_note: about 2 MiB, only while containers run
cap1: No containers yet: Docker's two daemons already run.
cap2: Three containers: a shim for each in Docker, one small keeper in podbag.
cap3: The containers stop: podbag's keeper leaves 10 seconds later.
cap4: No containers: Docker still holds 203 MiB. podbag runs nothing.
layers_sub: Other engines store images as layers. podbag stores them as files.
layers_b1: A layer store (Docker, Podman, Kiri) keeps a layer once only when the whole layer is the same. If one file differs, the whole layer is stored again, with the files it shares with other layers.
layers_b2: podbag keeps each file once. An image is a list of paths that point to the files.
layers_b3: For 8 Spring services in 2 releases: 902 MiB on disk against Docker's 2,970 MiB.
memory_text: When containers read the same file, the kernel keeps one copy of it in memory. With layers, the same file in two layers is two files, so it is read into memory twice. Starting 16 Spring services read this much into memory:

arch_alt: Docker Engine: the docker CLI talks to dockerd, which talks to containerd, which starts a shim per container; images are layers. podbag: the command creates each container itself, a keeper per user watches them while they run; images are files, each kept once.
intro_alt: podbag intro. Other engines keep daemons running; podbag runs only while containers run, and nothing at rest. Others store layers; podbag stores files, each once: 902 MiB of disk instead of 2,970 MiB for 8 Spring services in 2 releases, and 324 MiB of page cache instead of 982 MiB. A container starts in 4.1 ms, 18 times faster than Docker's 73.8 ms. Linux, macOS and Windows; podbag.dev.

perf_alt: How podbag compares with Docker, Podman and Kiri on one Linux VM: a container starts in 4.1 ms (Docker 73.8 ms); 100 containers hold 105 MiB (Docker 562 MiB); nothing runs with no containers (Docker 203 MiB); 8 Spring services in 2 releases take 902 MiB of disk (Docker 2,970 MiB) and 324 MiB of page cache (Docker 982 MiB).
